text:
incident-bot: PagerDuty P0 fired: private-vpc-controlplane-heartbeat-loss for customer AcmeCorp (region: eu-west-1) — heartbeat missing from on-prem agent fleet for 3x polling intervals. PD: https://pagerduty.example/alerts/P12345

pagerduty: Alert details: service=private-controlplane, urgency=high, impacted=AcmeCorp, symptom=agent-heartbeat-missing, last_heartbeat=2625000900, suggested_runbook=/runbooks/private-controlplane-heartbeat.md

maya_sre: ACK. I’m taking primary. joining bridge in 2m.

jamie_ops: I’m on-call too, joining bridge now. @maya_sre any known maintenance?

leah_support: CS notified AcmeCorp via email and Slack DM (ticket #INC-4123). Customer reporting increased 5xxs and model request timeouts since ~08:02 UTC.

alex_infra: quick triage: control plane pods appear healthy in cluster, but agent fleet for customer shows 'offline' in control-plane UI. hitting the agent host directly.

jamie_ops: running quick checks on one agent host:
```
$ ssh admin@10.11.12.33 
Last login: ...
$ sudo systemctl status redwood-agent
● redwood-agent.service - Redwood onprem agent
   Loaded: loaded (/etc/systemd/system/redwood-agent.service; enabled)
   Active: active (running) since ...
$ sudo journalctl -u redwood-agent -n 200 | tail -n 50
2026-03-14T08:00:45 AgentConnection - heartbeat timeout connecting to controlplane gateway 10.20.30.5:443
2026-03-14T08:01:46 AgentConnection - retrying, tls handshake failed: EOF
```

maya_sre: looks like agent -> control plane connectivity TLS/handshake failures. Could be customer network or local firewall/MTU. @tom_custeng can you confirm any recent network changes on your side?

tom_custeng: We haven't changed config, but we did see a maintenance window on our edge firewall earlier today. I'll check rule changes and MTU with our infra team now.

oncall-l2: I’m available to assist if we need host-level debugging or a config rollback.

jamie_ops: tried `curl -vk https://10.20.30.5:443/health` from agent host — TLS handshake fails with "alert handshake failure". Packet capture shows SYN/ACK then immediate RST from 10.20.30.1 (edge firewall).

alex_infra: escalating network suspicion. Short-term mitigation options: 1) restart agent (may restore session) 2) route traffic via fallback gateway in same region (requires control plane policy change) 3) request customer open firewall to allow controlplane IPs.

maya_sre: doing safety-first: will attempt agent restart on one host to see if re-registration works, then proceed one-by-one. Jamie's on it.

jamie_ops: running restart: `sudo systemctl restart redwood-agent`
```
$ sudo systemctl restart redwood-agent && sudo journalctl -u redwood-agent -n 50 --no-pager | tail -n 40
2026-03-14T08:07:12 AgentConnection - attempting TLS handshake to 10.20.30.5:443
2026-03-14T08:07:13 AgentConnection - connected, registration successful, heartbeat established
```

incident-bot: Note: agent 10.11.12.33 heartbeat restored at 2625001632.

leah_support: Updated ticket INC-4123: "We restarted one agent which re-registered successfully; customer still seeing intermittent 504s for some routes. CS asked customer to check edge firewall logs for RSTs."

maya_sre: Verified control-plane metrics: agent heartbeats reappearing, control plane latency back within SLO for this host. However, 3/12 agent hosts still show flaky handshakes. Need network team & customer to confirm.

alex_infra: I can provision a fallback gateway and apply a routing override for AcmeCorp to bypass the suspected firewall hop. That will take ~8-12 minutes and a brief config push. We should get customer approval first.

tom_custeng: Please do not reroute without our change control signoff. We will run a rapid check on firewall rules and MTU, reporting back in 10m.

maya_sre: fair. we'll hold on bulk reroute. continuing rolling restarts on remaining hosts but throttled to avoid flapping. tagging oncall-l2 for net-level pcap help.

oncall-l2: attaching a pcap snippet from 10.11.12.34 -> 10.20.30.5:443, shows MSS/MTU mismatch and repeated ICMP fragmentation-needed messages. suspect MTU of 1400 on intermediate device while path requires 1500.

jamie_ops: confirming when we `curl --path-as-is` with +MTU tweak we can TLS handshake succeed. Temporary workaround is to set PMTU discovery or lower agent MTU to 1400.

leah_support: Communicated workaround to customer: "We identified a likely MTU mismatch. Temporary mitigation options: apply PMTU fixes on your edge or allow our fallback gateway (requires your approval). We can also lower agent MTU remotely if you approve." Customer acknowledged and requested us to attempt agent-side MTU change as quickest path.

maya_sre: proceeding with staged MTU adjustment on two remaining flapping hosts (with rollback plan). updating runbook steps in /runbooks/private-controlplane-heartbeat.md to include MTU troubleshooting notes.

jamie_ops: applied MTU=1400 on 10.11.12.34 and 10.11.12.35. Both re-registered and heartbeats stable.
```
$ sudo ip link set dev eth0 mtu 1400
$ sudo systemctl restart redwood-agent
```

incident-bot: All known agents for AcmeCorp reported heartbeats restored at 2625003320. Alert status: resolved -> monitoring. PagerDuty: auto-resolve queued.

maya_sre: Post-mitigation status: control plane healthy, no new error spikes for 12m. Customer still performing validation on app traffic but reports reduction in 5xxs.

leah_support: Updated ticket INC-4123 and CC'd AcmeCorp network ops. Next action: CS to schedule a joint troubleshooting call to permanently fix MTU on their edge device.

oncall-l2: recommend follow-up action item: add MTU check to private agent onboarding checklist and add firewall/MTU verification to runbook.

maya_sre: Agreed. I'll create a short post-incident note and assign follow-ups: runbook update, onboarding checklist change, and a customer ops call. Tentatively closing incident in 30m if stable. :thumbsup:

jamie_ops: thanks everyone. monitoring channel for 30m.

leah_support: Customer ACK'd provisional resolution. Marking status as "mitigated" and waiting for customer confirmation before closure.

maya_sre: RESOLVED (mitigated). Root cause: likely MTU mismatch on customer edge firewall causing TLS handshake fragmentation failures. Permanent fix tracked in INC-4123 and follow-up ticket NET-789.

jamie_ops: closing thread, will reopen if anything recurs. :white_check_mark:
